facts.raw_span: a 2-year history of progressive abdominal distension
accompanied by early satiety and urinary urgency
denied pain, weight loss, or systemic symptoms
her menstrual cycles were normal
her mother had a history of ovarian cysts
the abdomen was distended with dull percussion notes but without tenderness or guarding
a cyst measuring 16 × 24 cm that compressed adjacent abdominal organs
a large midline intraperitoneal cyst, 30 × 25.6 × 16.8 cm in size, extending from the liver to the pelvis and involving the uterus and ovaries
the lesion had a fluid density of 20 Hounsfield units
demonstrated no calcifications, soft-tissue components, or enhancing septations, suggesting a benign etiology
laboratory studies, including α-fetoprotein, carcinoembryonic antigen, cancer antigen 19-9, and cancer antigen 125, were all within normal limits
the Risk of Malignancy Algorithm (ROMA) score was 4.1 %

concepts.why: The patient's mother had a history of ovarian cysts and the patient presented with a large midline intraperitoneal cyst involving the uterus and ovaries.
The patient presented with progressive abdominal distension and early satiety, which are common symptoms of a simple renal cyst.
The patient presented with a large midline intraperitoneal cyst that compressed adjacent abdominal organs, which is consistent with a mesenteric cyst.
The patient presented with a large midline intraperitoneal cyst that involved the uterus and ovaries, which is consistent with an omental cyst.

The patient presented with a large midline intraperitoneal cyst that demonstrated no calcifications, soft-tissue components, or enhancing septations, which is consistent with a peritoneal inclusion cyst.

The patient presented with a large midline intraperitoneal cyst that involved the uterus and ovaries, and had a low Risk of Malignancy Algorithm (ROMA) score, which is consistent with a mucinous cystadenoma.
The patient presented with a large midline intraperitoneal cyst that demonstrated no calcifications, soft-tissue components, or enhancing septations, which is consistent with a serous cystadenoma.
The patient presented with a large midline intraperitoneal cyst that involved the uterus and ovaries, which is consistent with a dermoid cyst.
